title: Microsoft Teams: user setting to stop presence switching to Do not disturb while screen sharing (GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and distinguishes the government-cloud release from the unqualified Microsoft Q&A guidance. The Teams licensing requirement is supported, and searches did not establish a default or an administrator switch for this opt-out. One checklist sentence should distinguish this setting from other documented presence controls.

claims.where: Governance controls: Client Do Not Disturb and Breakthrough
claims.claim: Learn says Teams administrators cannot currently customise the Client Do Not Disturb and Breakthrough settings discussed there.
claims.quote: Client Do Not Disturb and Breakthrough features are always enabled for users in Teams. ... The ability of a Teams admin to customize these settings isn't currently supported.

claims.claim: Users add people to a priority access list in Teams.
claims.quote: Users can add people to a priority access list by going to Settings > Privacy in Teams.

claims.claim: Users still receive calls from priority-access people while in Do not disturb.
claims.quote: Even if the user is in a Do not disturb state, the user still receives calls from these people.

claims.claim: Priority access is a separate user-side exception for callers, not an administrator control over the presenting opt-out.
claims.quote: Users can add people to a priority access list by going to Settings > Privacy in Teams. ... Even if the user is in a Do not disturb state, the user still receives calls from these people.
